source.note: Everyday first-century situations for a card's sentence to take place in. None is an episode or parable of the New Testament and none uses a New Testament name. ln_domains are the Louw-Nida domains a scene naturally involves, used to offer a vocabulary item settings its word belongs in. Drafted for review: prune or add freely.

scenes.scene: A potter's apprentice cracks a large jar just before the buyer arrives to collect it.
Two brothers argue over how to divide their late father's olive grove.
A widow bargains with a grain merchant in a year of poor harvest.
A fisherman's wife salts and packs the catch in jars to sell inland before it spoils.
A shepherd boy counts the flock at dusk and finds one lamb lame.
A travelling merchant's donkey refuses to cross a swollen stream.
A hired letter-writer in the market draws up a contract for two farmers who distrust each other.
A slave girl carrying water jars up steep steps drops one and fears her mistress's anger.
A carpenter and his neighbour dispute where a boundary wall should stand.
A mother nurses a feverish child through the night while the lamp burns low.
A young soldier on night watch at a city gate hears noises outside the walls.
A tax farmer's agent seizes a debtor's cart in the market.
An old teacher tests his pupils on the letters they copied onto wax tablets.
A household prepares a wedding feast and the cook runs short of salt.
A caravan waits outside a desert town while its leader bargains for water.
Two farmers watch the sky, hoping the rain holds off until the barley is in.
A baker's oven cracks on the morning of a festival.
A freedman returns to the house where he was once a slave to repay a debt.
A girl hides her brother's broken toy from their father.
An innkeeper and a traveller quarrel over the bill for feeding the traveller's mules.
A physician sets the broken arm of a stonemason who fell from scaffolding.
A council of village elders hears a complaint about a stolen goat.
A wine seller waters down his wine and a customer notices.
A boy sent to the next village with a message loses his way at night.
A household slave is freed in her master's will and must decide where to go.
A farmer's sons plant young olive trees that will not bear fruit for years.
Neighbours put out a kitchen fire before it spreads to the roof.
A merchant's ship waits in harbour for a favourable wind.
A grandmother teaches her granddaughter to weave a cloak.
A thief is caught climbing into a storeroom.
A young man writes a letter home asking his father for money.
A mother and daughter grind grain before dawn.
A goldsmith weighs a ring that a woman wants to pawn.
Workers repair a collapsed stretch of aqueduct under a foreman's eye.
A farmer's youngest son leaves home to enlist, and his mother packs his bag.
Two merchants swear an oath over a disputed shipment of wool.
A beekeeper is stung while moving his hives before winter.
A household mourns an old servant and prepares his burial.
A funeral procession passes a crowded market and the traders fall silent.
A boy steals pomegranates from a neighbour's garden and is chased off by the dog.
A leatherworker cuts sandals for a customer who keeps changing his mind.
An old man with swollen feet soaks them in warm water while his daughter scolds him.
Soldiers requisition a farmer's ox to haul their supplies.
A village celebrates the end of the grape harvest with music and dancing.
A young wife burns the bread on her first day in her husband's household.
An apprentice mason carves a name onto a gravestone and misspells it.
Two old friends meet after years apart at the city baths.
A steward counts the household stores before winter and finds the oil jars half empty.
A boat is caught in fog and the crew argue over which way the shore lies.
A girl learns to draw water with a rope and bucket without spilling it.
A blacksmith sharpens swords for the local garrison.
An old woman keeps the keys to the family storeroom and trusts no one with them.
A dog guards a vineyard at night against foxes.
Labourers clear stones from a field before the ploughing.
A family packs up to move to another city after a flood ruins their house.
The market inspector checks a merchant's scales.
A young man rehearses a speech he must give before the town council.
A judge hears two neighbours argue over a fallen wall.
A father teaches his son to read from a worn scroll of the family accounts.
A servant is sent to fetch a doctor in the middle of a storm.
A camel driver loses a load of pottery on a rocky path.
A mother bathes her infant and wraps him in warm cloth.
Children play at soldiers in the street with wooden swords.
A landlord raises the rent and his tenant farmer protests.
A lamp maker shows a customer new lamps with patterned handles.
A woman keeps watch at the bedside of her dying husband.
A traveller's sandal strap breaks on a mountain road far from the next town.
Two apprentices race to finish a table before their master returns.
A household slave overhears a plan to cheat his master.
Villagers gather to watch a surveyor mark the new boundaries of their fields.
A woman selling vegetables at the city gate argues over prices.
A household makes ready for the Sabbath at sunset and the lamp oil runs out.
A priest's servant carries baskets of offerings up the temple steps and drops one.
Pilgrims camp outside the city walls during a festival and quarrel over space.
A family fasts and prays for a grandmother who has fallen ill.
A convert is immersed in a ritual bath while his mother watches from the steps.
An old man teaches his grandson the blessing said before meals.
A sailor vows an offering to God if his ship reaches harbour safely.
Villagers say a demon haunts the abandoned tower on the hill.
A farmer and his sons pray for rain after a dry winter.
A merchant swears by God that his cloth is the finest in the city.
Two elders disagree over how the law applies to a borrowed ox that died.
A household gathers for the Passover meal and the youngest child asks the questions.
A synagogue attendant sweeps the floor early, before the town gathers.
Old men sitting in the gate argue over what an ancient prophecy meant.
A daughter reads her dead father's will aloud to the family.
A young man is ashamed to tell his parents he gambled away his wages.
A woman forgives the neighbour who borrowed her cooking pot and broke it.
A master forgives a slave who spilled a jar of costly oil.
Two brothers make peace at their mother's sickbed after years of silence.
A runaway slave hides in a hayloft and fears the dogs.
A household guard is bribed to leave a gate unbarred.
Debtors in a crowded cell share a single blanket through a cold night.
A shipowner hires sailors for one last voyage before the winter storms.
A girl chases the geese into their pen before a storm.
A farmer finds his neighbour's goats in his wheat and loses his temper.
A mother bargains for a warm cloak for her son before winter.
A king's messenger arrives in a village with news of new taxes.
A retired soldier teaches the village boys to march.
A doctor examines a slave for sale in the market and declares him sick.
A seamstress sewing a bride's garment runs out of thread.
A fisherman's hut floods when the lake rises.
Workers carry stones up to build the upper storey of a house.
A child falls asleep during a long evening meal and is carried to bed.
A dyer's hands are stained blue and his customers stare at them.
A tutor walks a wealthy boy to school and scolds him for dawdling.
A gravedigger and his son dig in rocky ground and break a spade.
An archer practises at a target while his friends mock him.
A potter shows his son how to centre the clay on the wheel.
Rain collapses a mud-brick wall and the family's sheep wander into the street.
A girl brings her grandfather his midday meal in the olive grove.
A servant carries a lamp ahead of his master along a dark street.
A cook is punished for burning a feast meant for important guests.
A tanner is shunned by his neighbours for the smell of his trade.
A father arranges his daughter's marriage and she objects.
A lender comes to collect and finds the family eating their last bread.
A cart wheel breaks on the road to market and the eggs are lost.
A hunter tracks a wild boar into the hills.
Three families share an olive press and argue over whose turn it is.
A night watchman sees a fire on the far hill and wakes the village.
A slave boy is punished for breaking his mistress's mirror.
An old sailor tells the children about a sea monster he claims to have seen.
A mother lays out clean clothes for her children on a festival morning.
A young man is made treasurer of a trade guild and the older members doubt him.
Two women carrying laundry to the river slip on the rocks.
An orphan girl is taken in by her uncle's family.
A schoolboy is beaten for failing to learn his lesson.
Snow blocks a mountain pass and a messenger has to turn back.
A craftsman carves a chair of state for a magistrate.
A guard dog barks all night and no one sleeps.
A family measures out the grain that must last them the coming months.
A court clerk reads out a sentence of exile.
A woman smells smoke and finds her neighbour's barn on fire.
A boy runs a race at the village festival and falls within sight of the finish.
Travellers shelter from the rain under a rock overhang and share what food they have.
A rich man's servants unload his furniture at a new house.
A moneylender counts his coins by lamplight.
A girl is afraid of the dark and sleeps beside her older sister.
A mule breaks loose in the market and scatters the fruit stalls.
A widow hires a man to mend her leaking roof before the rains.
A father and son walk to the city to sell a young calf.
The village well runs dry and the elders meet to decide what to do.
A guard is posted at the granary after grain goes missing.
An old woman tells her grandchildren about her own wedding day.
A man remembers too late that he promised to meet a friend.
A pupil contradicts his teacher and is sent out of the room.
A heavy rain washes away the newly sown seed.
A mother tells her son he must choose between the family trade and the army.
A boy learns that his friend lied to him about a borrowed knife.
A dispute over whether a debt was already repaid ends before the magistrate.
A family discovers that an heirloom cup is a clever fake.
A wealthy woman hides her jewellery in a wall niche as soldiers enter the city.
A child is too weak to climb the hill and his father carries him.
A pair of oxen cannot pull the cart out of the mud.
A wrestler trains for a match against a stronger man.
A household hurries to be ready before the guests arrive for a betrothal feast.
A carpenter measures the height of a doorway twice before cutting.
A caravan sets out east at dawn with the sun in their eyes.
A child seated in the middle of the table spills the soup.
A traveller leaves his pack with an innkeeper and goes on ahead.
A servant sets out the cushions in their places before the guests recline.
Two neighbours argue over whether one may draw water from the other's cistern.
A son finds he is bound to pay his late father's debts.
A host must seat his guests at a banquet without offending the older relatives.
A craftsman's work is praised in public and his rival is jealous.
A potter learns that a jar he sold cheaply was worth far more.
A merchant compares two bolts of cloth and cannot tell which is better.
A son takes up his father's trade and finishes his first piece of work.
A traveller must wait in a town until the bridge is repaired.
The rest of the family arrives a day after the first wagon.
A farmer divides his field into plots for his three sons.
A wine jar in the cellar is found empty and no one admits to it.
A household celebrates a daughter's recovery from a long illness.
A man bursts in with news that the river is flooding the lower fields.
A trader loses his purse and retraces his steps through the market.
A stonecutter splits a block and it cracks the wrong way.
A merchant's conscience troubles him after he cheats a child in the market.
A young woman's heart is torn between two suitors.
Two travellers argue over which road it would be wiser to take.
An old woman's shrewd advice saves a family's harvest.
A buyer refuses to believe the seller's word about a horse's age.
A boy shows his mother a hidden path he found through the reeds.
A merchant reveals his price only after the buyer has seen the goods.
A new apprentice follows the master builder everywhere and copies him.
Two rival fishing crews fight over the best stretch of shore.
A young man mends his ways after his father is shamed in the market.
Villagers keep an old custom of leaving bread at the crossroads.
A goatherd milks his goats at dawn.
A housekeeper hands out the day's tasks to the household slaves.
A servant pours water over the guests' hands before the meal.
The last traveller to arrive finds no food left.
A father learns that the gold ring he bought is genuine after all.
A shipwright repairs a damaged hull until it is fit to sail again.
A master trains a clumsy apprentice until he is fit to work alone.
A cook fires the ovens before dawn for a large order of bread.
The storeroom door sticks and will not open.
The spring grass withers in a hot wind.
A farmer ploughs the east field first because the sun dries it sooner.
A small boat is stuck in the middle of the river.
A mother calls her children in from the street for supper.
A foreman calls the workers to gather at the gate.
A workman's excuse for his absence proves to be empty.
A boy tastes the stew before the guests arrive.
A merchant obtains a permit to trade in the city.
A girl's handwriting looks just like her mother's.
A village grows into a town once the new road is built.
A well the village was promised for years is finally dug.
An earth tremor shakes the pots from the shelves.
A rower stretches out his hand to pull a swimmer aboard.
A kite snatches a fish from the drying racks.
A dockhand casts off the mooring ropes too early.
A family replaces their old cart with a new one.
Two potters' workshops turn out very different jars.
A fisherman's catch is so small he gives it away.
